newsitem.title: USA: Snyder sees 5 pct to 10 pct production rise.
newsitem.headline: Snyder sees 5 pct to 10 pct production rise.

text.p: Snyder Oil Co said Wednesday it expects oil and natural gas production to increase five percent to 10 percent in 1997, excluding acquisitions or exploration success.

The company said it has established a preliminary capital budget of $113 million for 1997, excluding acquisitions. This represents more than double the amount spent on development and exploration in 1996.
The increase, said Snyder, is due to growing opportunities in the Gulf of Mexico as well as a steady increase in development drilling in the Rockies given the rapid recovery in the gas market there.
Snyder said that reserve additions of 64.4 million barrels of oil equivalents (MMBOE) last year replaced 488 percent of 1996 production.

The increase, said the company, was driven by a combination of acquisitions, development drilling and exploration, paricularly in Colorado, Wyom,ing and the Giulf of Mexico. Snyder said its proved reserves at the end of 1996 reached a record 141.4 MMBOE, up 57 percent from the 90.2 MMBOE reported in 1995.
